pair1.note: This particular word ends up unchanged in the end (“mommy” in both the model's own raw pick and the post-fix-1 build's final output) — but for different reasons, and that's the real story here. The pre-fix build (838058e) had no re-validation loop at all: one guard check, one substitution, accepted immediately — it takes the first alternative (“mom”) and moves on. The post-fix-1 build (57ce25a) added a 4-pass re-validation loop as part of the same commit, but that loop didn't yet accumulate exclusions across passes (the bug 4c3a398 later fixed) — so it oscillates between “mom” and “mommy” for all 4 passes and, purely by landing on an even pass at the cap, ends up back on “mommy”. The word looks unchanged, but the mechanism that produced it already differs: this is the still-unfixed oscillation bug firing for the first time in this replay, several words before the visible “new new new new new” symptom — it just happens not to change the output here.

pair2.note: Before the second fix, remask_pick_excluding() only ever excludes the single most recent offender each pass, so across 4 passes it oscillates dog → cat → dog → cat and, at the pass cap, lands back on “dog” — reproducing the exact recurring bigram the guard exists to prevent. After the fix, the same guard call accumulates every rejected candidate across passes: pass 1 excludes “dog” and finds “cat”, which itself re-collides (the story already used “the cat”), so pass 2 excludes both “dog” and “cat” together and lands on a genuinely new word, “dog's”. Same collision, same first two candidates tried, but only the accumulated exclusion set lets the loop actually converge instead of cycling.
